country: # Wadden Sea spots lie in the national park: kite only in the marked zones

name: Sylt – Westerland
notes: Brandenburger Strand: Germany's main wave spot, strong current between the groynes. Experienced riders. Also: K4 by Hörnum (flat channels at low tide, waves at high tide); Hörnum Möwennest on the Wadden side for E winds (around low tide).

name: Sylt – List (Königshafen)
notes: Wadden Sea, shallow flat water. Nature reserve: launch only from the kite beach, ride inside the buoys, about 2–3 h either side of high tide.

name: Sankt Peter-Ording
notes: Ording beach (kite world cup venue): huge beach, flat to small waves, tide-dependent; strong current at times. Also: Büsum – Perlebucht further south (tidal lagoon, around high tide).

name: Cuxhaven – Kugelbake
notes: Elbe mouth: current and shipping lane. National park zone, about 3 h either side of high tide. Also: Sahlenburg west of town (large standing area, about 4 h either side of high tide).

name: Schillig
notes: Wadden Sea, shallow; ride around high tide. Kite school on site. Also: Hooksiel on the Jade further south (around high tide).

name: Norddeich
notes: Wadden Sea, kite area by the surf school; ride around high tide.

name: Norderney – Nordstrand
notes: Marked kite zone on the north beach; island rules limit the hours (not early morning). Also: Borkum and Langeoog north beaches (marked kite zones).

name: Flensburger Förde – Holnis
notes: Fjord spot, shallow near shore; marked kite zone in summer. Also: Schausende further out on the fjord.

name: Laboe
notes: Kiel Fjord mouth, shallow and flat near shore. Also: Stein 3 km east (about 200 m of standing area).

name: Heiligenhafen
notes: Steinwarder, east of the pier: wind waves, beginner zone in the shallows. Also: Großenbrode just east (flat water, small waves).

name: Fehmarn – Gold
notes: Huge shallow standing area, busy with schools; stones in the north part. Also: Lemkenhafen (Orther Reede) 3 km east, flat shallow water for S winds.

name: Fehmarn – Wulfener Hals
notes: Flat shallow water in the bay, small waves outside; best in E winds.

name: Fehmarn – Grüner Brink
notes: North coast: works in E winds when other spots are offshore; shared with a dog beach.

name: Pelzerhaken
notes: Long sandy beach, shallow; flat to small waves.

name: Salzhaff – Pepelow
notes: Salzhaff: shallow flat-water lagoon, ideal for learning.

name: Warnemünde
notes: Kite access at beach access 13, west of the pier; rough waves in strong N–NW wind.

name: Wustrow
notes: Baltic side: waves (German Kitesurf Open venue). Bodden side: flat shallow water. Also: Saal on the Saaler Bodden (flat shallow water, kite school).

name: Zingst
notes: Sportstrand at the edge of town; choppy, deep enough for foiling.

name: Rügen – Suhrendorf (Ummanz)
notes: Bodden: shallow flat water, beginner-friendly.

name: Rügen – Dranske
notes: Wieker Bodden side: flat water. Also: Wiek on the Wieker Bodden.

name: Usedom – Karlshagen
notes: Sportstrand with kite school; waves in E winds, W winds are offshore. Keep clear of the swimming zone. Also: Peenemünde just north; Ückeritz on the Achterwasser for W–S winds.

name: Steinhuder Meer
notes: Mardorf / Weißer Berg on the north shore: about 500 m of standing area. Kiting roughly 20 Mar–15 Nov in the marked zone.

name: Dümmer
notes: Shallow lake; launch at the surf entry point (Rohrdommel).

name: Chiemsee – Übersee (Feldwies)
notes: Kite zone at Feldwies on the south shore (Tiroler Achen delta): works in W–N winds. Kiting only in the marked zone. Also: Chieming on the east shore (KBC kite club zone, W–NW winds).
